source_text:
Ἀνεκαλύφθη καὶ τῆς
Μαγδαληνῆς Μαρίας ὁ λογισμὸς ἀσθενὴς ὤν· τοῦ Χριστοῦ σταυρωθέντος

ἠσθένησεν, ὅτε καὶ αὐτὴ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔλεγεν· «Κύριε, εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν, εἰπέ μοι
ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν, κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ.»
13 Τρεχέτω ἡ γλῶττα τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς ἱστορίας τὰ λείποντα· «Καὶ ἦν Ἅννα
προφῆτις, θυγάτηρ Φανουήλ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσήρ· αὕτη προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς,
ζήσασα μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἔτη ἑπτὰ ἀπὸ τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς, καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ὡς ἐτῶν
ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων.» Λαμπρὸς ὁ τῆς Ἅννης πλοῦτος, πανταχόθεν αὐτῇ ὁ τῶν
ἀγαθῶν θησαυρὸς συνάγεται, πρῶτον ὅτι προφῆτις ἦν· σκεῦος γὰρ ἀσθενὲς ὡς
γυναικεῖον ἔχουσα ἐκάθαιρεν αὐτό, καὶ τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ Πνεῦμα πρὸς αὐτὴν εἰς
κατοικίαν εἵλκυσεν· ἔπειτα ὅτι πρεσβῦτις ὑπῆρχεν καὶ τὸ σῶμα γηράσασα οὐκ ἐγήρα
τὸ φρόνημα· τρίτον ὅτι χήρα καὶ οὐχ ἁπλῶς χήρα, ἀλλ' ἔτη μὲν ἑπτὰ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῷ
ἀνδρὶ συμβιώσασα, προβεβηκυῖα δὲ ἡμέραις πολλαῖς καὶ χρόνοις τοσούτοις τὸν
ζυγὸν τῆς χηρείας ἕλκουσα, νυμφίῳ δευτέρῳ τὴν κοίτην οὐ προδέδωκεν, ἀνθ' ὅτου
ἄρα εἰς ἔτος ὀγδοηκοστὸν τοῦ βίου τὴν ἡλικίαν ἤλαυνεν.
14 Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ πάντως εἶδε τὸν ἐν τῷ ὀγδοηκοστῷ τετάρτῳ ψαλμῷ σαφῶς
τῷ Πνεύματι καταγγελθέντα, ἐζήτησεν εἰπεῖν περὶ αὐτοῦ τοιαῦτα οἷα ∆αυὶδ
προβάλλων ὁ ψαλμῳδὸς ἐμελῴδησεν· «Εὐδόκησας, κύριε, τὴν γῆν σου, ἀπέστρεψας
τὴν αἰχμαλωσίαν Ἰακώβ· ἀφῆκας τὰς ἀνομίας τῷ λαῷ σου, ἐκάλυψας πάσας τὰς
ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν. Κατέπαυσας πᾶσαν τὴν ὀργήν σου, ἀπέστρεψας ἀπὸ ὀργῆς θυμοῦ
σου. Ἀλήθεια ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἀνέτειλεν, καὶ δικαιοσύνη ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ διέκυψεν»· ἐν
τούτοις γὰρ «τῆς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἡ λύτρωσις», ἣν ἑξῆς οὕτως ἱστορεῖται καὶ κηρύξαι τὸ
γύναιον καὶ προφητεῦσαι· φησὶ γάρ· «ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ.» Πολλοὶ μὲν τὸ
ἱερὸν οἰκοῦσιν, ἀλλ' οἰκοῦντες ὑβρίζουσιν, ὅσοι οὐχ οὕτως οἰκοῦσιν καθάπερ ἡ
Ἅννα κατοικοῦσα ἐτύγχανεν, «νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ
ἡμέραν»· ταῖς μὲν γὰρ νηστείαις τὸ σῶμα ἐξεκάθαιρε, ταῖς δεήσεσιν δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς
ἀνεπτέρου τὸ φρόνημα καὶ ἱερὸν ἐν ἱερῷ κατοικοῦσα ἐτύγχανεν.
3
15 «Καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐπιστᾶσα»· πάντως γὰρ καὶ αὐτὴν τὸ Πνεῦμα καθάπερ
καὶ τὸν Συμεῶνα εἰς τὴν τοῦ βρέφους δοξολογίαν ἤγαγεν. «Ἀνθωμολογεῖτο τῷ
θεῷ»· οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐδοξολόγει ἀλλ' ἀνθωμολογεῖτο, τοῖς παρὰ τοῦ Συμεὼν εἰρημένοις
παραπλήσια ἀναφωνοῦσα. «Καὶ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς προσδεχομένοις
λύτρωσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.» Τίνα καὶ ποῖα λέγουσα; «Μὴ πλανᾶσθε τῇ σαρκί, τῇ τοῦ
δούλου μορφῇ μὴ προσκόπτετε, μὴ θορυβείτω τὸ βρέφος ὑμᾶς.» Ὁ τὰ βρέφη
διαπλάττων φαινόμενος καὶ παιδίον, νήπιον ὁ τῶν χρόνων πατὴρ ὁρώμενος· ἄλλως
γὰρ ἰδεῖν τὸν λυτρωτὴν οὐκ ἐχωροῦμεν, ἑτέρως οὐκ ἐδυνάμεθα δέξασθαι. Ἡμῶν
ἕνεκεν ἑαυτὸν ἐταπείνωσεν, δι' ἡμᾶς κατέβη· φειδοῖ τῶν ἡμετέρων ὀφθαλμῶν,
ἀποκρύπτει τὰ ἔνδοξα, τὰ ταπεινὰ προβάλλεται. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν
αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

4
thought_title: Anna's widowhood and proclamation of redemption
orientation: The preacher finishes showing how the cross reveals hidden thoughts, then turns to Anna's age, chastity and temple life and reconstructs her proclamation about the infant.
pass_a_gloss: And the thought of Mary Magdalene also was revealed, being weak; when Christ had been crucified she became weak, when she herself also was saying to him: ‘Lord, if you carried him, tell me where you laid him, and I will take him up.’ Let the tongue of the gospel history run through the remaining things: ‘And Anna was a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher; she advanced in many days, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity, and she herself a widow of about eighty-four years.’ Bright is the wealth of Anna, from every side the treasure of good things is gathered for her, first because she was a prophetess; for having a weak vessel as womanly she cleansed it, and she drew the Spirit of God to herself for a dwelling; next because she was an aged woman and having grown old in body she did not grow old in mind; third because a widow and not simply a widow, but having lived together with her husband seven years in number, and having advanced in many days and dragging the yoke of widowhood for so many years, she did not betray her bed to a second bridegroom, for which reason she was driving her age into the eightieth year of life. But since in every case she saw the one clearly announced by the Spirit in the eighty-fourth psalm, she sought to say about him such things as David the psalm singer putting forward sang: ‘You were pleased, lord, with your land, you turned back the captivity of Jacob; you forgave the lawless deeds to your people, you covered all their sins. You caused all your anger to cease, you turned back from the anger of your wrath. Truth sprang up out of the earth, and righteousness looked down out of heaven’; for in these things is ‘the redemption of Jerusalem,’ which next it is recorded in this way that the woman both proclaimed and prophesied; for it says: ‘who did not depart from the temple.’ Many dwell in the temple, but dwelling they outrage it, as many as do not dwell in the way Anna happened to dwell, ‘serving with fastings and prayers night and day’; for with the fastings she was cleansing the body, and with the prayers she was giving wings to the thought of her soul and she happened to dwell as temple in temple. ‘And having stood by in that very hour’; for in every case the Spirit also led her just as also Simeon to the praise of the infant. ‘She was giving thanks in return to God’; she was not simply giving praise but she was giving thanks in return, crying out things like the things said by Simeon. ‘And she was speaking about him to all those awaiting redemption in Jerusalem.’ Saying what and what kind of things? ‘Do not be led astray by the flesh, do not stumble at the form of a servant, let the infant not trouble you.’ He who fashions infants appearing even as a child, seen as a baby he who is father of the ages; for otherwise we could not contain to see the redeemer, in another way we could not receive him. For our sake he humbled himself, for us he came down; he spares our eyes, he hides the glorious things, he puts forward the lowly things. To him be the glory into the ages of the ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: inner thought here revealed as weak
became weak in faith after crucifixion
gave thanks in return, answering praise

choices.why: keeps singular λογισμός distinct from plural διαλογισμοί in brief and keeps literal weakness, not doctrinal unbelief
required by brief glossary sense of woman prophet applied to Anna
preserves anti- prefix force of answering Simeon's words, not generic praise
required by brief glossary for Jerusalem proclamation

choices.term: τῇ τοῦ δούλου μορφῇ μὴ προσκόπτετε
choices.english: do not stumble at the form of a servant
choices.why: keeps literal stumbling image and lowly form, not abstract offense
rejected: do not take offense at his servile appearance

pass_b_english: Mary Magdalene’s thought lay open too, and it was weak. Her thought grew weak after Christ was crucified. She spoke to him without knowing him and said, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away” (John 20:15).

Let the Gospel story run on and supply what remains. Luke says, “And Anna was a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was far advanced in days, having lived with her husband seven years from her virginity, and she was a widow of about eighty-four years” (Luke 2:36) (Luke 2:37).

Anna’s wealth shines bright. Her store of good things gathers from every side. First, she was a prophetess. She bore a frail vessel, a woman’s body, and she cleansed it. She drew the Spirit of God to dwell in her. Second, she was aged, and though her body had grown old, her resolve had not grown old. Third, she was a widow, and no ordinary widow. She lived only seven years with her husband. She advanced many days and dragged the yoke of widowhood through so many years. She never gave her bed to a second bridegroom. So she drove her life into its eightieth year.

She had seen him whom the Spirit clearly proclaimed in the eighty-fourth psalm. So she longed to speak of him in words like those David the psalmist sang: “Lord, you favored your land; you turned back the captivity of Jacob. You forgave the iniquities of your people; you covered all their sins. You stilled all your anger; you turned away from your fierce wrath” (Psalms 85:1-3); “Truth has sprung from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven” (Psalms 85:11). In these words lies the redemption of Jerusalem, which Luke next says this woman proclaimed and prophesied. For Luke says, “She did not leave the temple” (Luke 2:37). Many live in the temple, yet living there they insult it. They do not dwell as Anna dwelt, “serving night and day with fasts and prayers” (Luke 2:37). By fasting she cleansed her body. By prayer she gave wings to her soul. She dwelt as a temple within the temple.

Luke adds, “And coming up at that very hour” (Luke 2:38). The Spirit surely brought her, as it brought Simeon, to praise the infant. Luke says, “She was giving thanks in return to God” (Luke 2:38). She was not merely praising. She was answering God with praise, crying out words much like Simeon’s. Luke says, “And she spoke of him to all who were awaiting redemption in Jerusalem” (Luke 2:38). What was she saying? “Do not be led astray by his flesh. Do not stumble at the form of a servant. Do not let the infant trouble you.”

He fashions infants, yet he appears as an infant and a child. He is seen as a babe, yet he is the Father of ages. We could not have beheld the Redeemer otherwise. We could not have received him otherwise. For our sake he humbled himself. For our sake he came down. He spares our eyes. He hides his glory and puts forward his lowliness. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
